analysis: Examined units: (1) Test harness changes. PlacementChecks/Main.swift head line 66 adds checkGemmaTensorParallel. run.sh head lines 87-89 compile Gemma4TensorParallelPlan, QwenTensorParallelLaunch and Gemma4TensorParallelRequestBudget into the model-free check binary. New GemmaTensorParallelPlanCheck.swift and gemma-run.sh are offline developer checks against repository safetensors header JSON. They use mktemp plus a trap cleanup and do not use the network, MLX or provider secrets. Force-casts on repository inputs only affect test crashes. None of this ships in the provider runtime, so it adds no attack surface relevant to TB-002, TB-003 or TB-007. (2) The libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule moves from 7933a0fa to a4f67fa5. The submodule diff is not supplied. It is the in-process inference engine (TB-007, T-028, T-041 KV/prefix handling, T-008 fail-closed behavior), so the content of this bump is unreviewed. This is a coverage limit, not evidence of a regression. (3) In DistributedResidentExecution.swift, head line 88 replaces the inline supportsLogprobs predicate with ClusterModelFeaturePolicy.capturesLogprobs(capability, mode:). Base lines 87-90 granted logprobs only in tensorParallel mode, for the glm5NextLayerStage adapter or for adapters where servesQwenTensorLanes is true. The new policy implementation is not supplied. If it widens this set, for example to the new Gemma tensor-parallel adapter or to non-TP modes, a request with topLogprobs>0 would pass refusal() at base line 374. If that runtime does not actually capture logprobs, the request could fail or return mismatched logprob data (availability/correctness, A-001 integrity). Integration should verify that ClusterModelFeaturePolicy.capturesLogprobs: (a) keeps the tensorParallel-only restriction; (b) fails closed for unknown adapter IDs; (c) stays aligned with NativeWorkerRuntime.capturesLogprobs, including for any newly added Gemma TP adapter. Integration should also check the Gemma4TensorParallelPlan runtime sources, which are compiled here but not supplied, for how they handle untrusted config/header input when loading on provider peers. No concrete regression is identified from the visible evidence.
